newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's first multicultural old age home opens.
newsitem.headline: Germany's first multicultural old age home opens.

text.p: Germany's first multicultural old age home, with facilities for both German and Turkish pensioners, opened on Monday in the Ruhr valley industrial city of Duisburg.

The home, run by the German Red Cross (DRK), has a Moslem prayer room and three Turkish nurses in addition to its normal facilities including a Christian chapel, a spokeswoman said. Some of the German staff have also learned Turkish.

Germany, which invited workers from southern Europe and Turkey to help man its factories in the 1960s, now has over 350,000 foreign pensioners who have stayed on rather than return to their countries of origin.
Officials expect that number to climb to over 1.7 million by the year 2010, creating far more demand for multicultural facilities in old age homes and hospitals.

Relations between Germans and the 1.9 million Turks living here have been strained in recent years by xenophobic attacks and Bonn's refusal to grant immigrants dual citizenship. But there are also many grass-roots projects to foster better understanding.

DRK spokeswoman Angelika Witjes-Hielen said it was unusual for Turkish families to turn to old age homes. "Most families still stick to tradition and say the old people will stay in the family," she said.
But many Turkish pensioners realised they would not return home and their children, most of whom were born here and speak German fluently, could not always take care of them, she added.
"In terms of the care they need, a 70-year-old Turk is about 10 years older on average than a 70-year-old German because of the hard work he did," she said.
